❗️Damaging winds and heavy rainfall is expected over the Central Phillipines amid the landfall of typhoon Kalmaegi Monday night❗️

Forecasts by region for the Phillipines: 

Eastern Visayas: 
Typhoon conditions are expected from 7:00 pm Monday evening until 8:00 am Tuesday over southern sections. 
Hazards: 
• Wind gusts: 120 to 140km/h except locally up to 190km/h near Suluan. Winds will be less severe over northern sections. 
• Rainfall amounts: 50 to 100 mm except locally more then 200 mm over southern sections

Central Visayas: 
Typhoon conditions are possible from 1:00 am until 9:00 am Tuesday. 
Hazards: 
• Wind gusts 100 to 130km/h except locally 150km/h over northern sections
• Rainfall amounts: 150 to 250 mm

Western Visayas:
Typhoon conditions are expected from 7 am Tuesday until 7:00 pm. 

Hazards: 
• Wind gusts: 120 to 140km/h except 150 to 170km/h over exposed shores
• Rainfall amounts 150 to 250 mm over southern sections, 50 to 100 mm over northern sections. 

Mimaropa: 
Typhoon conditions are possible over northern sections from 11:00 pm Tuesday until 7:00 am Wednesday. 
Hazards: 
• Wind gusts: Up to 140km/h over northern sections 
• Rainfall amounts: Up to 350 mm over northern sections

For the remainder of the central Phillipines, heavy rainfall and tropical storm force winds are expected at times Monday night into Tuesday night, beginning and ending a bit later over the western sections. 
Those located in the Visayas regions are advised to be prepared for destructive wind gusts locally ranging 150 to 200km/h Monday night. 
Severe flooding is possible locally and landslides are expected in areas of steep terrain. 
Consider moving to a storm shelter, especially over the southeastern Visayas coast. Prepare for evacuation orders. 

The next forecast will be posted by 12:30 pm Phillipines time today. 

Kalmaegi is forecast to exit the Philippines  Tuesday night, and the storm is expected to intensify into a T5 storm, possibly even reaching T6 status, with sustained winds 190-220km/h. 

Both the North and the South Central Coast Regions of Vietnam are advised to postpone travel plans for Nov 6-7th. 

Please stay updated on the most recent forecasts. #Typhoon #Phillipines #TyphoonKalmaegi #Storm #Vietnam
